claim_updates.reason: No change to claim status from parent HYPOTHESIS. The frozen falsifier C1 triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING: all four estimators (weighted PMI, equal-weight PMI, median PMI, KNN CMI k=5 alpha=1.0) fail the null control (|null_mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000 on the 12-state hash-routed SPA: 0.407, 0.704, 0.686, 0.262 bits respectively, each 2.6-7.0x threshold and 32-56 sigma from threshold). The bias-corrected estimator pathway (equal-weight, median, KNN) is rejected as a remedy in this setting. The preregistered mechanistic hypothesis H1 (bias from large-stratum dominance) is falsified: equal-weight and median null bias is WORSE than weighted (0.704/0.686 vs 0.407 bits) because per-stratum plug-in bias is monotonically increasing in small strata (+0.742 bits at size 5-9 vs +0.379 at size 20-49), and equal-weighting/median promote the most biased strata. KNN shows negative bias (-0.262 bits) from Laplace smoothing + extra dimension. No estimator converges at N=50000 (all drift >0.2 bits). C-WEB-DYNAMICS concerns real Web dynamics; all evidence remains synthetic in-memory SPA simulation. The K3-K2 beyond-Markov question is unanswered (no valid estimator exists), not answered in the negative.

next_question: Does SPA redesign with 0% deterministic strata (all transitions stochastic) eliminate the per-stratum plug-in PMI null bias on stochastic strata, where the bias persists at +0.742 bits even for strata of size 5-9 under the shuffled-action null — and does this redesign enable a valid beyond-Markov test, or is the bias intrinsic to plug-in estimation regardless of determinism ratio?
